summary: NGFW clipping long HTTP/2 DATA frames causes gRPC streaming truncation on Private deployment
description: Customer reports intermittent truncated chat responses and spurious 401 refresh errors for long-running streaming chat sessions from their Private deployment. Issue appears only when a stream exceeds ~30s or when a single HTTP/2 DATA frame size goes above ~64KB. Behavior started after a corporate NGFW firmware update on customer side.
impact: Multiple production customers at FinVault Bank observe partial model outputs and streaming disconnects during lengthy assistant responses. Transactions that rely on streaming completions fail and require user retry; estimated ~12% of long-form generation requests affected during peak windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy Private agent with VPCE endpoint to FinVault VPC (prod, us-west-2).
2) Call /v1/chat/stream with system+user prompt that triggers a long generation (>30s or >64KB DATA frames).
3) Observe stream ends unexpectedly with 'stream closed by remote' and subsequent control-plane 401s when client attempts token refresh.
4) Re-run capture with tcpdump on customer host and on Redwood-facing edge to compare tcpdump captures.
logs: client: grpc StatusCode=14 desc=stream terminated by server: EOF
serving-node: 2026-03-10T14:12:04Z WARN streaming: upstream reset by peer (RST), session_id=abcd-1234
control-plane: 2026-03-10T14:12:05Z ERROR auth: token refresh failed: unexpected EOF while reading OCSP response
ngfw-capture.txt: see packet capture; middlebox injects RST immediately after a large HTTP/2 DATA sequence (frame length ~65536).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 15:00 - Support: Confirmed issue only for long streams or large HTTP/2 frames; short responses unaffected.
2026-03-10 15:30 - Customer (FinVault): Noted NGFW firmware pushed last night (PAN-OS 11.2.3) and a new HTTP/2 accelerator/inspection feature enabled in default rule set.

2026-03-10 16:00 - SRE captured simultaneous tcpdumps on customer bastion and Redwood edge. Diffs indicate packets with large HTTP/2 DATA segments are being clipped mid-stream by NGFW; NGFW then sends TCP RST back to both endpoints.

2026-03-10 16:20 - Packet analysis: RSTs originate from NGFW IP, not from NAT gateway. When NGFW clips frame the downstream serving node receives a truncated H2 frame which triggers internal parsing error and session tear-down.

2026-03-10 17:00 - Hypothesis: NGFW HTTP/2 inspection engine has an internal reassembly buffer limit (64KB) and incorrectly treats overflow as malformed traffic, triggering connection termination. Explains correlation with firmware push.
2026-03-11 09:00 - Reproduced in lab by enabling 'http2-deep-inspection' feature on a Palo Alto test appliance (PAN-OS 11.2.3) — appliance clipped DATA frames >64KB and reset connection.
workaround: Customer disabled HTTP/2 application inspection for traffic to Redwood VPCE CIDRs and increased TCP idle/flow timeout on the NGFW rules covering the agent. After bypassing inspection, streams remain stable. Recommended short-term: add explicit bypass rule for Redwood control-plane and serving IP ranges and disable 'http2-deep-inspection' on those rules.
resolution: Pending: Customer accepted workaround and applied bypass policy in their NGFW. Support to monitor for 48 hours. Long-term options: we will add explicit guidance to Private deployment onboarding recommending NGFW bypass or configuring inspection to allow large HTTP/2 frames. Engineering will track a telemetry flag to detect RSTs originating from middleboxes and produce clearer diagnostics. Follow-up action: create a KB article and update runbook.
comments: Customer (J. Mercer, FinVault): 'We pushed PAN-OS last night as part of holiday patching. After rollback to previous snapshot streams recovered.'

Support (Aisha Patel): 'Thanks — can you confirm exact rule id and whether NAT or proxy is in path? A packet capture would help; saw your pcap uploaded to s3://finvault-support/pcaps/2026-03-10.pcap.'

Support (Aisha Patel): 'Provided CIDR list and runbook link; advised to keep bypass rule scoped to VPCE ENIs only and to avoid broad internet-wide bypasses.'
